name: Loch Fyne Scottish Smoked D Cut Salmon, 1kg
desc: Product Details After filleting (which takes place in the local village of Cairndow), the classic smoked salmon is dry cured for 24 hours and then smoked with oak chips for a further 12 -15 hours at ambient temperature. It's this process that gives Loch Fyne classic smoked salmon its delicate yet distinctive flavour. D-cut is a slicing technique that gives the salmon slice a 'D' shape. It involves slicing the fish from back to belly. This includes the salmon’s rich, flavoursome brown meat. Each slice is then carefully layered on top of each other, in order to recreate the look of the original, uncut side. The D-cut side is the perfect way to buy smoked salmon if you’re entertaining. Serve with brown bread, butter and fresh lemon for a simple, tasty dish made easy. Loch Fyne Oysters Ltd. was established in 1978 by local landowner Johnny Noble and his friend, marine biologist Andy Lane. The company started with the inspirational idea of growing oysters in the clean, fertile waters at the head of Loch Fyne – the longest sea loch in Scotland - providing both employment for locals and income to support the estate at Ardkinglas. Using their combined knowledge and enthusiasm, they laid the foundations for the company to become one of Scotland’s foremost producers of premium seafood and the home of our internationally acclaimed restaurant – proud to have served celebrities, film stars, Prime Ministers and even Royalty. Today, Loch Fyne has evolved to include not only the original oyster farm, restaurant and deli but also an award winning smokehouse, mussel farm and oyster hatchery. Loch Fyne’s philosophy, ‘Nach Urramach an Cuan’ (How worthy of honour is the sea), encapsulates the way they run their companies - enterprise with respect for animals, people and ecology. Commitment to independent producers using sustainable methods to produce high quality foods. Loch Fyne are passionate about delivering quality and flavour, making where they source their produce the key. They make sure that every oyster harvested, every salmon prepared and every fish leaving their shops and kitchens is cultivated, farmed or fished in accordance with their strict environmental and quality guidelines, taking advice from respected marine bodies. Where species are not plentiful they find alternatives and do not source fish caught by methods deemed to be harmful to the marine ecosystem such as deep-sea trawlers, beam trawlers or industrial long-liners. When buying Loch Fyne, you can be assured that all their products are sourced according to quality, provenance and sustainability. desc: Product Details This Traditional BBQ box contains the essentials to make sure no-one at your Summer event will go hungry! This Box Includes: Joyce & Charles Ashbridge (mother and son) founded Taste Tradition on New Year's Day 2004. Their success is testament to the increased value people place on animal welfare, traditional methods and high quality, beautifully tasting real produce. Nestled near the top of Sutton Bank in the North York Moors National Park, the Ashbridge family have farmed in Cold Kirby for three generations. The traditional methods of breeding, rearing and finishing livestock used in our grandfather's day are still evident in Charles's farming protocols. The cattle are rare or traditional breeds, with the majority being Longhorn, Shorthorn, Belted Galloway, Dexter, Aberdeen Angus and Hereford Red Poll. These breeds take longer to mature, and require extensive farming. However, the marbling this produces in the meat and the flavours on the palate are well worth the effort! They have a grass-based diet, which is what cattle have traditionally consumed for centuries. This diet leads to a magnificent creamy-soft yellow coloured fat, which is high in Omega 3 oils. One of the lesser known health benefits of grass-fed, traditional breed meat is this high level of Omega 3 oils. The burgers are 100% rare or traditional breed beef, nothing is added to the mix which allows you to add salt, pepper or any seasoning of your choice whilst cooking. Using the best cuts of well aged rare breed beef allows the flavour of the meat to speak for itself. All of their pork at Taste Tradition is of rare or traditional breed origin, typically Gloucester Old Spot, Saddleback, Berkshire, Middle White and Large Black. These breeds carry an extra bit of fat which helps to infuse moisture and a superbly distinctive flavour into the meat whilst it cooks. The pigs consume natural feed, which is a factor responsible for the high quality and flavour of the pork that they produce. The sows usually produce two litters (9-11 piglets) per year, and are left to furrow unattended in their own outdoor huts. Specialist rations have been formulated which are free of GM products and are always enjoyed by Taste Tradition pigs. When the time comes, these cattle and pigs are taken to a local abattoir, avoiding the stress of a long journey. The bodies of these cattle are then hung in their maturation chiller, on the bone, for between 21 and 28 days. Taste Tradition have full traceability from the farm, through the slaughterhouse to delivery to the customer.
